title: Grapefruit Juice Flavanones Modulate the Expression of Genes Regulating Inflammation, Cell Interactions and Vascular Function in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells of Postmenopausal Women.
authors: Krga, Irena; Corral-Jara, Karla Fabiola; Barber-Chamoux, Nicolas; Dubray, Claude; Morand, Christine; Milenkovic, Dragan
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过多组学分析探究葡萄柚汁黄烷酮对绝经后女性PBMC基因表达的影响，并用分子对接预测黄烷酮代谢物与转录因子（如STAT3、NF-kappaB）的结合，虽涉及TF-DNA互作但非核心，方法以实验和简单对接为主，深度有限。
abstract: Grapefruit is a rich source of flavanones, phytochemicals suggested excreting vasculoprotective effects. We previously showed that flavanones in grapefruit juice (GFJ) reduced postmenopausal women's pulse-wave velocity (PWV), a measure of arterial stiffness. However, mechanisms of flavanone action in humans are largely unknown. This study aimed to decipher molecular mechanisms of flavanones by multi-omics analysis in PBMCs of volunteers consuming GFJ and flavanone-free control drink for 6 months. Modulated genes and microRNAs (miRNAs) were identified using microarrays. Bioinformatics analyses assessed their functions, interactions and correlations with previously observed changes in PWV. GFJ modified gene and miRNA expressions. Integrated analysis of modulated genes and miRNA-target genes suggests regulation of inflammation, immune response, cell interaction and mobility. Bioinformatics identified putative mediators of the observed nutrigenomic effect (STAT3, NF-kappaB) and molecular docking demonstrated potential binding of flavanone metabolites to transcription factors and cell-signaling proteins. We also observed 34 significant correlations between changes in gene expression and PWV. Moreover, global gene expression was negatively correlated with gene expression profiles in arterial stiffness and hypertension. This study revealed molecular mechanisms underlying vasculoprotective effects of flavanones, including interactions with transcription factors and gene and miRNA expression changes that inversely correlate with gene expression profiles associated with cardiovascular risk factors. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: [ClinicalTrials.gov], identifier [NCT01272167].
abstract_zh: 葡萄柚是黄烷酮的丰富来源，这些植物化学物质被认为具有血管保护作用。我们先前的研究表明，葡萄柚汁（GFJ）中的黄烷酮可降低绝经后女性的脉搏波速度（PWV），这是动脉僵硬度的一个指标。然而，黄烷酮在人体内的作用机制在很大程度上尚不清楚。本研究旨在通过对饮用GFJ和无黄烷酮对照饮料6个月的志愿者外周血单核细胞（PBMCs）进行多组学分析，来解析黄烷酮的分子机制。使用微阵列技术鉴定了受调控的基因和微小RNA（miRNAs）。生物信息学分析评估了它们的功能、相互作用以及与先前观察到的PWV变化的相关性。GFJ改变了基因和miRNA的表达。对受调控基因和miRNA靶基因的综合分析表明，其涉及炎症、免疫反应、细胞相互作用和移动性的调控。生物信息学分析识别了观察到的营养基因组学效应的推定介导因子（STAT3、NF-kappaB），分子对接显示黄烷酮代谢物与转录因子和细胞信号蛋白存在潜在结合。我们还观察到基因表达变化与PWV之间有34个显著相关性。此外，全局基因表达与动脉僵硬度及高血压的基因表达谱呈负相关。本研究揭示了黄烷酮血管保护作用的分子机制，包括与转录因子的相互作用，以及与心血管风险因素相关的基因表达谱呈负相关的基因和miRNA表达变化。临床试验注册：[ClinicalTrials.gov]，标识号[NCT01272167]。
